title: Common chunks and filtered approximation of Dwyer--Kan limit cones
statement:
Use combinatorial simplicial model categories and projective enriched diagram models of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and Dwyer--Kan homotopy limits and enriched localizations of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small in the following hypotheses means $\mathcal U$-small, and the full model category and the indexing collections of subcategories are allowed to fit in $\mathcal U'$. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category and $(I_a)_{a\in A}$ a small family of small cofibrant simplicial categories. A chunk $U\subseteq\mathcal M$ means a full simplicial subcategory with these closure properties, with choices functorial by enriched functors: every finite fan $X\to Y_i$ in $U$ has a factorization $X\to Z\to\prod_iY_i$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration with $Z\in U$, and every finite cofan $Y_i\to X$ has a factorization $\coprod_iY_i\to Z\to X$ as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration with $Z\in U$; empty families are included. For a small simplicial category $I$, $U^I$ denotes the full enriched subcategory of $\mathcal M^I$ of diagrams valued in $U$. An $I$-chunk means that $U$ is a chunk and $U^I$ is a chunk in the projective model structure.

Fix a small partially ordered set $K_0$. There is an infinite regular $\mathcal U$-small cardinal $\kappa$, which can be chosen depending only on $K_0$ and the Kan model on simplicial sets for the homotopy-limit clause below, with the following simultaneous approximation property. There is a $\mathcal U'$-small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered collection of small full subcategories $U_\lambda\subseteq\mathcal M$, each a common $I_a$-chunk, whose union is $\mathcal M$. Here $\kappa$-filtered means that every subcollection of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has an upper bound. The collection can be required to be $\mu$-filtered for any prescribed infinite regular $\mathcal U$-small $\mu\geq\kappa$. For every $a$, full inclusions of subcategories induce a canonical Dwyer--Kan equivalence
$$\operatorname{colim}_\lambda\bigl(U_\lambda^{I_a}\cap(\mathcal M^{I_a})^f\bigr)[W_{\lambda,a}^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M^{I_a})^f[W_a^{-1}],$$
where all the distinguished arrows are objectwise weak equivalences. The comparison is natural under enriched restriction between the $I_a$ and uses the actual restriction functors on fibrant diagrams.

Moreover the class of homotopy limit cones of shape $K_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ in $\mathrm{sCat}$ is stable under $\kappa$-filtered pointwise colimits: if $H_\lambda:K_0^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sCat}$ and compatible cones $Z_\lambda\to H_\lambda$ are homotopy limit cones, then $\operatorname{colim}_\lambda Z_\lambda\to\operatorname{colim}_\lambda H_\lambda$ is a homotopy limit cone. The cardinal bound for this closure remains valid when the ambient universe is enlarged. Neither this assertion nor the approximation identifies simplicial categories with infinity categories.

The localization comparison is the filtered-union step of that proof, using functorial enriched localization. Read online on 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.
